To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) sortilin is an important regulator of atherosclerosis that functions independent of lipoprotein metabolism; 2) sortilin is a receptor for proinflammatory cytokine IL-6; 3) sortilin-deficient mice have reduced secretion of proinflammatory cytokin IL-6 and reduced atherosclerosis; and 4) sortilin is required in immune cells for atherosclerosis.

sortilin regulates the development of atheroscleromatic lesions, independent of its effects on lipoprotein metabolism; sortilin regulates the secretion of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL- 6 and IFN-gamma; and targeting of sortilin in immune cell reduces atherogenesis and markers of inflammation.
sortilin is required for cytokine signaling in atherosclerosis, and that targeting sortiln in immune cells reduces atherosclerosis.
